papers.title: A two-scale approach for efficient on-the-fly operator assembly in massively parallel high performance multigrid codes
papers.abstract: Matrix-free finite element implementations of massively parallel geometric multigrid save memory and are often significantly faster than implementations using classical sparse matrix techniques. They are especially well suited for hierarchical hybrid grids on polyhedral domains. In the case of constant coefficients all fine grid node stencils in the interior of a coarse macro element are equal. However, for non-polyhedral domains the situation changes. Then even for the Laplace operator, the non-linear element mapping leads to fine grid stencils that can vary from grid point to grid point. This observation motivates a new two-scale approach that exploits a piecewise polynomial approximation of the fine grid operator with respect to the coarse mesh size. The low-cost evaluation of these surrogate polynomials results in an efficient stencil assembly on-the-fly for non-polyhedral domains that can be significantly more efficient than matrix-free techniques that are based on an element-wise assembly. The performance analysis and additional hardware-aware code optimizations are based on the Execution-Cache-Memory model. Several aspects such as two-scale a priori error bounds and double discretization techniques are presented. Weak and strong scaling results illustrate the benefits of the new technique when used within large scale PDE solvers.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文不涉及代理模型、不确定性量化或生物力学设计，仅关注高性能计算中的多重网格刚度矩阵组装的加速方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address surrogate modeling for expensive simulations, does not handle constraints or uncertainty quantification, and is not applied to implant/biomechanics design.

summary_zh.motivation: 加速非多面体域上大规模并行有限元中刚度矩阵的在线组装。
summary_zh.method: 提出一种两尺度方法，利用粗网格上的多项式逼近细网格算子，从而通过低代价评估实现快速组装。
summary_zh.result: 该方法在弱扩展和强扩展测试中均表现出优于传统基于单元组装的效果。
summary_zh.validation: 通过执行-缓存-内存模型进行性能分析，并给出弱扩展和强扩展数值结果。

summary_en.motivation: Efficient on-the-fly stencil assembly for matrix-free multigrid solvers on non-polyhedral domains.
summary_en.method: A two-scale approach that approximates fine-grid operators with piecewise polynomials on coarse macro elements, enabling low-cost evaluation.
summary_en.result: The surrogate-based assembly outperforms element-wise matrix-free techniques in both weak and strong scaling tests.
summary_en.validation: Performance analysis using the Execution-Cache-Memory model and numerical scaling results on large-scale parallel systems.

papers.title: Study of Material Densification of In718 in the Higher Throughput Parameter Regime
papers.abstract: Selective Laser Melting (SLM) is a powder bed fusion additive manufacturing process used increasingly in the aerospace industry to reduce the cost, weight, and fabrication time for complex propulsion components. Previous optimization studies for SLM using the Concept Laser M1 and M2 machines at NASA Marshall Space Flight Center have centered on machine default parameters. The objective of this project is to characterize how heat treatment affects density and porosity from a microscopic point of view. This is performs using higher throughput parameters (a previously unexplored region of the manufacturing operating envelope for this application) on material consolidation. Density blocks were analyzed to explore the relationship between build parameters (laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing) and material consolidation (assessed in terms of density and porosity). The study also considers the impact of post-processing, specifically hot isostatic pressing and heat treatment, as well as deposition pattern on material consolidation in the higher energy parameter regime. Metallurgical evaluation of specimens will also be presented. This work will contribute to creating a knowledge base (understanding material behavior in all ranges of the AM equipment operating envelope) that is critical to transitioning AM from the custom low rate production sphere it currently occupies to the world of mass high rate production, where parts are fabricated at a rapid rate with confidence that they will meet or exceed all stringent functional requirements for spaceflight hardware. These studies will also provide important data on the sensitivity of material consolidation to process parameters that will inform the design and development of future flight articles using SLM.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究高产量参数下Inconel 718的致密化行为及热处理影响。
summary_zh.method: 通过改变激光功率、扫描速度和间距进行密度块分析，并应用HIP和热处理。
summary_zh.result: 表征了参数与致密化的关系，但未提供力学性能或生物医学相关性。
summary_zh.validation: 基于密度和孔隙率的金相评估。

summary_en.motivation: To characterize densification and porosity of Inconel 718 fabricated by SLM under higher throughput parameters.
summary_en.method: Density blocks were analyzed by varying laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing, with post-processing including HIP and heat treatment.
summary_en.result: The relationship between process parameters and material consolidation was established, but no mechanical or biomedical properties were assessed.
summary_en.validation: Metallurgical evaluation of density and porosity.
